_help.about: The torch (design 30 Sept §AW): a burning brand carried in one hand, the first tool. Unlit until held to a flame (a lit fire, a planted torch, another torch); burns about one night; a point light with Minecraft-style falloff; can be planted in the ground. Restart after editing.
_help.burn_min: Real minutes a torch burns at full flame (the equatorial night is 48).
_help.gutter_share: The last share of its life it spends guttering: dimmer, harder flicker, the warning to head for a fire.
_help.rain_burn_scale: Burn-time multiplier in rain (storm: storm_burn_scale). douse_depth_m: water this deep puts it out.
_help.light: range_m / energy / attenuation: the falloff. gutter_energy: energy while guttering. flicker_hz / flicker_amount / wind_flicker_scale: the old flame's flicker, no longer read since the torch's head became an ember (§CP, 3 Oct): it breathes with its coal instead (see ember). sprint_flicker_scale is still read: sprinting feeds the coal air (ember.air_brighten). shadows false: no shadow map from a torch (§AG).
_help.planted: Right click the ground with a lit torch to stand it up; take it back within pickup_reach_m.
_help.lighting_reach_m: How close to a flame the torch must be held to light.
_help.bundle: Unlit torches by a camp's fire (§AW): how many, and how many game hours until the folk have made more.
_help.climb: Starting a climb with a lit torch plants it if there is ground to plant it in, otherwise it goes out (stowing puts it out; relight at a flame).
_help.resin: The resin torch's block (technique resin_torch): see resin._note.
_help.swing: (design §CN) The swing passes the flame. Left click (button: the item-in-hand action, "shoot") with the torch in hand swings it: the bare-hand swing's arc and timing (fists.gd, use_fist_arc), with the torch in the hand. At the end of the arc the flame passes between whatever it touches within reach_m (the same as lighting_reach_m), lit to unlit, either way (passes_flame): a lit torch lights a laid fire (fuel.json kindling), embers, a laid delve fire-holder (delves.json) or a planted torch (lights); an unlit torch swung through a lit fire, a lit fire-holder or a planted torch catches (takes_from). Sharing a flame costs the torch nothing (share_cost_min 0): its own burn is still the clock. It never lights the ground, standing grass, camp structures, folk or creatures (never_lights): wildfire's ignition stays a torch dropped in dry grass (§BL). A swing at a creature does nothing (creature_effect none): they answer to fire, not to the swing (§BA). Supersedes §AW's lighting ritual and the old hearths' right click (right_click_lights false): right click goes back to plain interact. log: the lines it adds to the log (§AZ).
_help.ember: (design §CP, recorded; built 3 Oct, Mike: "instead of the current fire animation, more of a glowing ember") The held and planted torches carry no flame: their head is the burnt end of the stick, amended the same afternoon (Mike: "not a ball"; built b7ebed5; shaders/torch_ember.gdshader); the lamps and every fire keep their flames. texels_m: texels a metre on the burnt end. crawl: how fast its cracks crawl. pulse_hz / pulse_amount: its slow breath, which the light's energy follows (Torch.ember_glow). shimmer_hz / shimmer_amount: a faint quicker shimmer on top. air_brighten: how much sprinting and wind brighten it. gutter_glow: the coal's glow while guttering (cooler). These are the code's own defaults, written down here; the code reads this block.
_help.kinds: [NOT WIRED YET — design §CQ] Every torch is from somewhere. The folk make each camp's bundle (bundle, §AW) in tiers (kinds.bundle): first the camp's own people's light (data/peoples/*.json light: the first entry that is a kind's technique and whose genera grow where the camp stands, by the same gate as fuel.json kindling, §CA; where_no_genus names what that people uses instead, e.g. the lake folk's reed twist where no birch grows); else a torch tree that grows there (tree_kinds; the commonest within camps.json sim.loop.gather_reach_m if more than one, then tree_kinds order); else the plain brand, the torch as built. list: circle_scale scales light.range_m (the circle the dark keeps out of, dread.json torch_circle); burn_scale scales burn_min; energy_scale scales light.energy; rain_immune: rain does not shorten it (only the kinds made of fuel.json kindling's wet_ok kinds, §CN; rain_why where no genus says so); storm_burn_scale replaces the top-level one for that kind; dip: the resin_torch technique can dip it, and a dipped torch becomes resin, which keeps its numbers in the resin block (numbers_in) and adds only its circle here. technique: the techniques.json id that teaches the kind (a people's light). made: what it is, from the peoples fill. First guesses by Claude (chat), 3 Oct; the designer owns them. Check: tools/torch_kinds_check.py.
_help.ember_relight: [NOT WIRED YET — design §CQ] A carried coal brings a dead torch back. With an unlit torch in hand (relights: any with burn left, such as one that went out in water or when it was put away, or a spare from a bundle; not a burnt-out stick) and a live coal carried (the ember carrier's ember item, technique ember_carrier, one at a time as built), one press of button blows the coal into the torch: after takes_s it catches with the burn it had left, and the coal is spent (spends_coal). cancel_if: sprinting or swimming stops it. button: Claude Code's call within §CN's scheme (right click is interact): planting needs a lit torch, so this does not collide with it, and a fire in reach keeps its own interact. log: the line it adds (§AZ). Fire is never made, only carried: the coal came from a hearth (§BP).
_help.snuff: [NOT WIRED YET — design §ET.7] The torch is forgiving: walking, turning and looking about never put it out (walking_and_looking). It goes out only in rare, dramatic moments, and each warns first with the coal guttering (warns_first). sprint: a flat-out sprint held for gutter_after_s seconds starts the gutter; held to out_after_s it goes out; stop sprinting during the gutter and the coal recovers over recover_s. draft: drafts blow from the builders' airways (§ET.6). An ordinary draft only leans the flame and gutters it (lean_only). A strong draft puts it out, but strong drafts are placed by the generator at marked airway mouths, never rolled at random (strong_at); each is heard and seen coming (a rising moan, dust or smoke streaming) warn_s seconds ahead, and stepping out of its line or behind cover in that time keeps the torch lit (shelter). water: deep water still douses it, at douse_depth_m as before (§AW). Out means out: relight at a lit hearth, a relit fire-holder or a carried coal (§CQ). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; Mike tunes by playing.

light._help_held_scale: Design 4 Oct §EB.3 (added by Claude Code): the torch in hand's energy and range times this (about 25-30% brighter, same colour), so it pushes the dark back further; planted torches keep range_m and energy. First guess; Mike tunes it by playing.
light._help_shadows: Not read since design 6 Oct §ER.1 (Claude Code): a torch casts a soft shadow only while it is among the nearest fire lights (look.json fire_shadows, FireShadows).

resin._note: Design 30 Sept §BP resin torch (technique resin_torch): dipped in pine pitch it burns burn_scale times as long, energy_scale as bright, shrugs off drizzle (rain_immune) and only a storm shortens it. First guesses by Claude Code 1 Oct; the designer owns them.

log.kindling_wet: The kindling smokes and won't catch.

brand.name: Torch
brand.made: A brand of the local wood: the torch as built (§AW). Where no one's light and no torch tree fits, the folk leave these.

fatwood.name: Fatwood splints
fatwood.made: Resin-soaked heartwood split from an old pine stump (Douglas-fir pitchwood in the temperate rainforest, §CN): long and bright, and it lights wet. The taiga and old-growth folk's, and any camp's among pines.

birch_bark.name: Birch-bark torch
birch_bark.made: Strips of birch bark wedged in a split pole: a big, smoky, quick flame, and its oils keep water out (§CN). The lake folk's (their fishing torch, carried), and any camp's among birches.

candlenut.name: Candlenut string
candlenut.made: Oil-rich nuts strung on a rib, burning one after another: a small, steady light that lasts. The tropical-forest and mangrove folk's. The candlenut tree is not in the catalogue yet (§CQ), so none are made until it is added.

dammar.name: Dammar torch
dammar.made: Dipterocarp resin pounded and packed into a leaf or bark tube: a slow, bright hand light in the wet forests. The canopy folk's. Rain still shortens it: no source yet shows dammar burning damp (§CN).

fir_candle.name: Fir candle
fir_candle.rain_why: Bog pine root is fatwood: resin-soaked heartwood that lights wet (fuel.json kindling fatwood_shavings, §CN).
fir_candle.made: Thin splints of resin-black pine root dug from the peat face: hot and bright. The marsh folk's.

ichu.name: Ichu grass torch
ichu.made: A tight twist of dry tussock grass bound with grass cord: short and bright, and it dies in the wind. The highland folk's.

cane.name: Cane torch
cane.made: Dry cane, reed or bamboo bound in a bundle: bright and fast. The karst folk's, and the lake folk's reed twist where no birch grows.

rushlight.name: Rushlight
rushlight.made: A peeled rush drawn through tallow, wedged in a split stick: small, cheap and steady. The mountain folk's.

fire_stick.name: Fire stick
fire_stick.made: A twist of cured grass or a dry thorn branch carried burning at arm's length: it burns out in minutes. The savanna herders'.

resin.name: Resin torch
resin.made: The pitch dip (technique resin_torch, built, §BP): a brand or a birch-bark torch dipped at a conifer. Its burn, brightness and rain rules stay in the resin block; this adds only its circle.

log.caught: The torch caught from the coal.
